messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: 3 containers restarted on gpu-pool-3 due to GPU OOM during prefill. Affected model: redwood-13b-quant. Trace: oom_kill, SIGKILL. Paging @dani-oncall :rotating_light:

incident-bot: /cluster/gpu-pool-3 reports repeated restarts (3x) in 12m, avg restart interval ~4m. Top symptom: large prefill sequences (>=120k tokens) from a small set of users.

dani-oncall: I'm on it. grabbing logs now. Anyone seen a correlated deploy?

ryan-sre: no deploys showing in last 30m. I can jump in for node-level checks. point me to logs you have.

maya-runtime: seeing a pattern. Prefill phase memory spike -> nvml reports OOM -> container restarted by kube with reason "OOMKilled". Prefill requests are coming in with really long history + embeddings precompute.

dani-oncall: paste some logs:

```
Dec 14 12:03:12 gpu-node-17 kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 23456 (redwood-inf) score 123 or sacrifice child
Dec 14 12:03:12 containerd: container "abc123" terminated with exit code 137 (OOM)
nvml: GPU 0: out of memory while allocating 16GB for KV cache
```

ryan-sre: ok. node memory looks fine, it's GPU memory exhaustion. Could be a single huge prefill (long prompt) saturating KV cache and spilling into other containers.

cathy-cs: any customer impact? We got a ticket from AcmeCorp complaining generator errors at 12:04.

maya-runtime: yes, requests from that tenant hit failures when routed to gpu-pool-3. Some requests retried and succeeded on different nodes but with latency spike.

dani-oncall: immediate mitigations?

ryan-sre: short-term: cordon gpu-node-17 to stop new pods. Add taint or scale up GPU nodes. Also enable a temporary routing policy to exclude gpu-pool-3.

maya-runtime: I can flip a routing rule to avoid gpu-pool-3 and roll out a model-variant fallback (redwood-13b-quant-8bit) for heavy-context requests. That variant uses smaller KV cache.

leo-eng: also we can enable prefill trimming for requests over 64k tokens. We have a feature flag `prefill_trim_threshold` that trims oldest context when prefill > threshold. I can flip it to 64k globally for 15m.

dani-oncall: do it. Start with routing exclusion + prefill trim + cordon. Post commands here.

ryan-sre: cordon and drain (graceful) commands:

```
# cordon the node
kubectl cordon gpu-node-17
# evict non-system pods, allow critical scheduling
kubectl drain gpu-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

ryan-sre: done cordon. node un-schedulable. Evictions in progress, some containers already restarted on other nodes.

maya-runtime: routing rule flipped to avoid gpu-pool-3 for redwood-13b-quant heavy-context requests. Model fallback for existing in-flight large requests enabled: `redwood-13b-quant-8bit`.

leo-eng: prefill_trim_threshold set to 64k and enabled (flag: `prefill_trim_mode=drop_oldest`). I also pushed a quick guard that rejects prefill > 200k tokens with 413 to avoid pathological clients.

cathy-cs: Sent an interim message to AcmeCorp: "we're investigating GPU OOM causing restarts; we've routed traffic away from the affected pool and are applying mitigations. We'll follow up with timeline and impact details."

incident-bot: NOTE: automated rollback guard triggered for redwood-13b-quant model in gpu-pool-3 routing.

ryan-sre: watching metrics. GPU memory pressure on pool dropped from 95% -> 40% after routing change. Pod restarts have stopped in the last 6m.

dani-oncall: good. Can we confirm root cause? Long-running prefill from a small set of users or a misbehaving client?

maya-runtime: digging through request traces. Found repeated pattern: a single client session sending multi-part chat history with embeddings and full-document prefetching. Prefill size often 150k-240k tokens. That overwhelms KV cache allocation and the runtime tries to allocate per-layer KV buffers causing OOM.

leo-eng: that's consistent. The runtime assumes worst-case KV cache allocation proportionate to prefill length unless `prefill_trim` is set. Also noticed no `max_prefill_tokens` enforced on that tenant due to an older onboarding rule.

dani-oncall: action items?

maya-runtime: short-term (now): keep routing exclusion on gpu-pool-3 until nodes drained and rebooted. Keep prefill_trim at 64k. Enforce tenant-level `max_prefill_tokens=100k` for the tenant causing the issue.

leo-eng: mid-term (hours): push a runtime change to opportunistically share KV cache across requests (soft cap) and improve allocation failure handling to fall back to streaming prefill instead of allocating full KV. I'll prepare a patch but won't deploy immediately.

ryan-sre: infra action: replace gpu-node-17 (possible stuck GPU driver state). I'll reimage it and run stress tests before uncordoning.

cathy-cs: I'll prepare a customer update: timeline + mitigation + ETA for full resolution. Please add impact numbers (requests failed, customers affected).

dani-oncall: current impact: ~120 failed requests over 12m, primary affected tenant: AcmeCorp (12 requests failed). Most other traffic retried successfully. No data loss, only transient errors and increased latency on rerouted requests.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied: node cordoned, routing exclusions active, prefill_trim set, model fallback enabled, tenant max_prefill enforced. Monitoring for 30m.

ryan-sre: node reimage started. Reimage will take ~25m.

leo-eng: patch is being drafted in branch `runtime/kv-failover`. I'll share PR for review (not deploying during incident).

cathy-cs: sent customer update to AcmeCorp at 12:35 PT: "We routed your traffic away from affected GPU pool and applied temporary limits on prefill size. Expect normal behavior now; please reopen if you see issues."

dani-oncall: any follow-ups for postmortem?

maya-runtime: postmortem items: enforce tenant-level prefill caps on onboarding, add a runtime guard to reject >200k prefills earlier, make prefill_trim default for large contexts, and add an alert when a single client/session generates >100k prefill tokens per minute.

ryan-sre: infra PM: consider autoscaling GPU nodes faster on sudden long-prefill surges and detect nodes with repeated OOM kills (healthcheck).

leo-eng: I'll link the PR and a small perf test that reproduces behavior (script included) in the postmortem doc.

dani-oncall: closing loop: no new restarts in 22m, node reimage progressing. We'll keep routing exclusion for 1h extra then reevaluate. If stable, we'll uncordon and reintroduce node gradually.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: After mitigations and node reimage, no further OOM restarts observed for 1h. Follow-up: create postmortem and customer-facing incident summary.

cathy-cs: customer notified with final summary at 14:10 PT.

dani-oncall: thanks all. adding postmortem owners: leo-eng (runtime fix), ryan-sre (infra follow-up), cathy-cs (customer comms).

sre-bot: Reminder: create PagerDuty incident and add timeline + signal graphs.
